newsitem.title: USA: Calif. candy scare proves unfounded - police.
newsitem.headline: Calif. candy scare proves unfounded - police.

text.p: A candy tampering scare in California proved unfounded when police said late on Friday that initial tests showing a 7-year-old boy had been poisoned with cocaine on Halloween were wrong.
Police said Ferdinan Siquig was out with family and friends in San Jose on Thursday night when he collapsed after eating candy and cookies he was given while "trick-or-treating."
(Children, typically in costume, go door-to-door for candy and other treats on Halloween.)

Siquig was taken to a local hospital where urine analysis revealed traces of cocaine in his system, leading authorities to say he was given a cocaine-laced treat, San Jose police spokesman Louis Quezada said earlier.
Six detectives were assigned to the case.

However, when the blood and urine samples were sent to an outside laboratory for a more thorough analysis, test results showed no drugs in the boy's system. Hospital staff also concluded that their initial test results were wrong, police said in a statement.
Police said the boy appeared to have fully recovered. It was not known why he collapsed but it did not appear to be related to the candy he ate.
